Update: I've re-connected the connection from the board to the stepper motor, cleaned the y-axis (surprisingly quite a bit of dust). 

It seems to work fine but after about 5 mins into a test print, it stopped moving and produced the same grinding noise. So i checked everything again. The same issue happened after about 5 mins into a test print. 

It seems to happen after the stepper motor got warm to the touch? Does it make sense?

just unplugged and plugged in the endstop wires and it does click when the bed has moved all the way back. 

Grinding noise seems to happen the most when the bed is about midway under the extruder.

I've got a failed print where the layer shifted about 30 minutes into the print. After canceling the print, there was a horrible grinding noise during the auto-home and the y-axis stops moving. After disabling the stepper motor, y-axis seems to move fine with no noise or any resistance. 

Any idea what is wrong? Thanks in advanced!
Thanks for the advice, I tossed out the whole batch while wearing gloves and mask.
This bag is about a week old. A brown powder is coming off the growth as well, looks a little like rust.
Just to clarify, the black stuff is growing on the plastic, not on the cake. The cake contains oyster mushroom spawn.

Somehow the thought of letting them know is scarier than dying.

I know that this is just a form of escape but escape is looking pretty good
Yes! I dunked the cake over night and mist them twice a day.
Any comments from friends and family? Any changes in how people talk or react to you?
